messages:
maya: heads-up — noticed ~15-25ms p50 increase on SSE streaming after today's deploy (deploy c3f9a) during canary. p95 also up. anyone else?
ryan: saw it during the morning smoke. chunk spacing looks different, tool-call endpoints showing higher serialize time. starting a bisect.
sam: perf-bot flagged CI job streaming_latency_synthetic failing on linux-aarch64, job: https://ci/internal/1234
maya: bisect narrowed to commit 7f2b1a in service-proto: 'sse: coalesce small frames into single message v2'. reverting locally removes the regression.
jo: can you paste the perf profile / flame? what's the top hotspot?
ryan: quick profile snapshot: ```
p99 latency: before 68ms -> after 94ms
hotspots:
 - proto.Encode (toolcall serialization) +12ms
 - stream.FlushCoordinator.wait +8ms
 - kernel_select: more frequent small-batch path
```
maya: looks like the coalesce change added an outer JSON envelope for tool-calls which increases encode cost and prevents incremental flushes. that also makes the runtime choose small-batch kernels more often -> worse perf.
sam: proposed actions:
 1) revert 7f2b1a on canary now
 2) add microbench for proto.Encode with toolcall payloads
 3) add SSE e2e asserting max-frame-delay and ensure incremental flush behavior
 4) add CI perf guard for streaming_latency_synthetic
jo: any compatibility risk from reverting? will clients depend on coalesced frames?
maya: it's an internal server optimization; clients should be unaffected. still, we'll double-check. @ryan can add details in the PR description.
ryan: creating revert PR now: PR #5589 — includes perf test and a small unit that asserts no extra envelope.
perf-bot: CI alert: streaming_latency_synthetic flake count increased x5 over last 24h. test-run: 98765
maya: holding rollout across regions and reverting canary. pinging infra to stop the rollout.
sam: stopping rollout in orchestration dashboard :thumbsup: (done). @perf-bot please add this to oncall queue.
jo: also saw increased KV cache miss rate in the same window — small-batch behavior likely thrashes the cache. adding KV microtest to the list.
maya: thanks all. if revert doesn't fully restore numbers, next plan is to tweak kernel selection heuristics and add a small-batch synthetic to CI to catch regressions early.
ryan: confirmed locally: after revert p50 back to ~64ms, p95 back towards baseline. pushing PR and will request urgent review. :rocket:
